grades.quote: If both bits are clear, no additional ordering constraints are imposed on the atomic memory operation. If only the _aq_ bit is set, the atomic memory operation is treated as an _acquire_ access, i.e., no following memory operations on this RISC-V hart can be observed to take place before the acquire memory operation.
grades.reason: States that RISC-V has a relaxed memory model and that an atomic op with both aq and rl clear imposes no additional ordering. It also explains that aq gives acquire semantics (the lock-acquire case) and rl gives release semantics. So an atomic-based lock needs ordering bits or fences to order the critical section.
Describes which atomic operations (LR/SC, AMOs) a memory region supports. It says nothing about memory ordering or barriers in locks.
Covers process memory protection and privilege modes. It is unrelated to atomic locks and memory barriers.

grades.quote: since the parent releases locks, and the child acquires locks as it starts up, the memory barriers in acquire and release ensure that the child’s CPU sees the parent’s writes.
grades.reason: Says that lock acquire and release in xv6 on RISC-V include memory barriers. These barriers make one CPU's writes visible to another, which shows locks need barriers beyond the atomic operation itself. It is not an explicit statement that atomics alone are insufficient.
